Election Presidential Gubernatorial Imam Murthada Gusau
All praise belongs to Allah, the Owner of absolute Dominion. He gives power to whom He wills, and He strips power from whom He wills. He exalts whom He wills, and He abases whom He wills. In His Hand is all good.
Dear servants of Allah! Please, look at the soil beneath your feet. This rich, resilient Nigerian earth has outlived empires, colonial masters, military regimes, and democratic administrations.
Respected brothers and sisters! The enduring reality is that Nigeria—as a land, a collective soul, and a divine trust and amanah—is immeasurably bigger, greater, and more permanent than any politician, leader, or transient power broker. While leaders come and go like shifting shadows, the land and its people remain accountable to a higher cosmic order.
Sincerely speaking, politicians are merely brief tenants on a land owned entirely by the Creator, Allah. They occupy offices for a few short years, but the consequences of their stewardship — and the collective destiny of over 200 million souls — endure long after they are gone.
Allah Almighty warns us in the Noble Qur’an about the intoxicating nature of worldly power and wealth, He says:
“Know that the life of this world is but amusement and diversion and adornment and boasting to one another and competition in increase of wealth and children…” [Qur’an, 57:20]
Follow us on Google News and never miss breaking stories, investigations, and in-depth reporting.
When a politician walks the corridors of power, surrounded by sirens, wealth, and praise, psychology tells us they often fall into the trap of the “hubris syndrome.” They begin to believe that the nation cannot survive without them. But the religion of Islam shatters this illusion through ascetic teachings.
Lets ask ourselves, where is Pharaoh today? Where is Qarun? Where are the powerful monarchs of yesterday? They entered the earth with nothing but a shroud, leaving behind a legacy that is either cursed or blessed. Nigeria will not fall because a politician fails; Nigeria belongs to Allah, and its people are its true heartbeat.
Dear Muslim believers! We must shift our mindset from political dependency to spiritual agency. We have elevated flawed, mortal men to the status of national architects, forgetting that true change begins within our own psychological and spiritual architecture.
We complain about corruption, yet we participate in micro-corruption in our marketplaces, in our schools, and in our offices. A nation is simply a mirror of its collective souls. If we want a greater Nigeria, we must realise that our duty to this land is a religious obligation.
“Each of you is a shepherd, and each of you is responsible for his flock.” [Sahih Al-Bukhari]
Fellow brothers and sisters! Nigeria’s rivers, forests, mineral wealth, and brilliant minds are blessings we will be questioned about on the Day of Judgment. Some politicians use ethnic and religious fault lines to divide us for temporary electoral gains. Wallahi, to succumb to this is a sign of spiritual disease. Our strength does not come from Aso Rock Villa; it comes from the sweat of the market woman in Kano, the brilliance of the tech youth in Lagos, the endurance of the farmer in Benue, Zamfara, Kogi etc, and the prayers of the righteous people across this land.
Imagine a billionaire politician who held the fate of millions in his hands. He signed budgets, decided who ate and who starved, and walked with an army of guards. Now, fast forward a few decades. He lies in a quiet, dark grave in a local cemetery. The sirens are gone. The wealth is distributed. The political parties have moved on to new faces.
Above his grave, the ordinary citizens of Nigeria—the ones he ignored—continue to walk, to build, to live, and to survive.
Here who was bigger? The man who thought he owned the country, or the country that swallowed him back into its soil?
Nigeria is an idea etched into the divine decree. It is a tapestry of over 250 ethnicities woven together by Allah’s wisdom. Allah Almighty says:
“O mankind, indeed We have created you from male and female and made you peoples and tribes that you may know one another…” [Qur’an, 49:13]
Fellow servants of Allah! To move from emotional reflection to real-world activation, every Nigerian citizen must adopt three spiritual-psychological shifts as follows:
Stop treating elected officials as masters. In Islam, the leader is the servant of the people, The Khadimul-Ummah. Hold them accountable, but never tie your hope, your livelihood, or your patriotism to their names.
Despair is a sin. The moment you say “Nigeria can never change,” you have doubted Allah’s power to transform hearts. Keep building, keep educating, and keep doing good in your immediate circle.
On the day of elections or civic duties, sell not your soul for a bag of rice, sphagetti or petty cash. Wallahi, that momentary transaction paralyses the future of your children. Act as a guardian of the amanah.
O Nigerians! Lift your head high. Know that, governments will rise and fall. Policies will change. Budgets will be spent. But your faith, your resilience, your unity, and your devotion to the Almighty Allah are unshakeable. Do not let transient men ruin a permanent blessing. Build your homes on righteousness, raise your children with integrity, and remember that this giant of Africa is held up by the hands of the Almighty Allah, not the whims of politicians.
Dear brothers and sisters! Fear Allah, and know that power belongs solely to Al-Malik, The True Sovereign.
And know that, our great country Nigeria is an enduring trust and amanah from Allah, a vast land of millions of souls, and an estate far greater than the fleeting shadow of any single politician.
We look at our nation today and see a people consumed by the names of men. We anchor our hopes, our anger, and our entire futures to individual politicians—mortals who breathe the same air we breathe, who sleep, who err, and who will inevitably return to the dust.
Respected brothers and sisters! Politicians are but brief actors on a stage. They are transient. They occupy an office for four years, eight years, or a lifetime, and then they disappear into the pages of history. But Nigeria—with its over 200 million souls, its innocent children, its hardworking mothers, its resilient youth, and its spiritual heritage—is a sacred trust.
Therefore, do not trade your brotherhood, your peace, or your eternal soul for the temporary ambitions of a mortal leader. When politicians stoke the fires of division, remember that they are small, but the collective destiny of this Ummah and this nation under Allah is immense. Nigeria is bigger than any politician’s ambition.
My dear brothers and sisters! Look at the reality of this world through the lens of Zuhd and asceticism. The Prophet Muhammad (Peace be upon him) said:
“What have I to do with this world? The relation between me and this world is like a traveler who sits under the shade of a tree and then walks away and leaves it.” [Tirmidhi]
If this entire world is just a temporary shade, what then is the seat of a governor, a senator, a president, a house of representative member, a state assembly member, a local government chairman or a councillor? It is a shadow within a shadow.
Please, why do we allow our hearts to be broken by their failures? Why do we allow our communities to be fractured by their campaigns? Why do we bleed for men who do not know our names?
Fellow Nigerians! Remember, a politician is just one person. But Nigeria is a tapestry of millions of prayers rising to the heavens every single night. Please, do not elevate a servant to the status of a master. Your loyalty belongs to Allah, and your duty of care belongs to your neighbours, your community, and your country.
There is a profound lesson from our righteous predecessors, as-Salafus Salih. A powerful leader once rode through his kingdom in grand pomp, surrounded by bodyguards, demanding total subservience. He passed by a wise, ascetic Islamic scholar sitting in the dirt. The leader demanded:
“Yes. I know your beginning and your end. Your beginning was a dropped drop of fluid, and your end will be a decaying corpse in the earth. And between the two, you are merely carrying waste.”
Let this be our reminder when we look at the political landscape of Nigeria. No matter how loud a politician’s convoy, no matter how vast their wealth, they will face the Grave alone. The land they rule over will outlive them. The people they govern will survive them. The nation is the canvas; the politician is merely a passing drop of ink.
Awaken, Nigeria citizens and Muslim believers! Stop waiting for a political messiah to save Nigeria. The salvation of our nation lies in the reformation of our own hearts, our honesty in our marketplaces, our kindness to our neighbours, and our collective turning back to Allah Almighty.
Wallahi, a politician cannot fix a home where character has decayed. A politician cannot bring peace to a community that has abandoned justice.
Nigeria will stand long after the current political elite are forgotten names in a textbook. Protect the nation, serve the people, and fear none but Allah Subhanahu wa Ta’ala!
Dear servants of Allah! When the Prophet Muhammad (Peace be upon him) was forced to leave his birthplace, Makkah, he stood at the edge of the city, looked back with tears in his eyes, and declared:
“How sweet you are as a land, and how dear you are to me! If my people had not driven me out from you, I would not have dwelt anywhere else.” [Tirmidhi]
This is not mere sentimentality; it is a divine template. The spiritual heart does not exist in a vacuum. It is rooted in the soil that sustains it. To love Nigeria, to prioritise its survival, and to labour for its resurrection is a direct expression of the values taught by Islam. You cannot claim to love the Creator if you actively despise or destroy the cradle of His creation in which He placed you.
Our collective suffering—the economic hardship, the insecurity, the fracturing of social trust—is a material reflection of a deeper spiritual drought. The Noble Qur’an provides an unyielding psychological law. Allah Almighty says:
“Indeed, Allah will not change the condition of a population until they change what is in themselves.” [Qur’an, 13:11]
We have fallen into the trap of looking outward for saviours while harbouring the very diseases that collapse nations from within: greed, selfishness, mutual distrust, apathy, and the pursuit of individual survival at the expense of the collective.
A nation is nothing more than the sum of its individual souls. If we are corrupt in our small daily transactions, our leadership will inevitably reflect that collective deficit. The reform of Nigeria does not begin at the Eagle Square in Abuja; it begins in the quiet chambers of your own conscience.
Do not forget! Nigeria is a trust and amanah from Allah. Every resource, every citizen, and every public space is an amanah. Betraying the nation through bribery and corruption, through cutting corners, through nepotism or tribalism is a direct betrayal of this divine trust.
Stop asking what Nigeria can do for you when the soil is parched. Ask what you are pouring into the ground. And please, before you point fingers at the leadership, audit your own integrity in your workplace, in your home, and in your community.
Also despair is a spiritual failure. To claim Nigeria is beyond redemption is to limit the mercy and power of Allah Almighty. We must actively cultivate hope as a form of resistance against chaos.
There is a profound lesson in the classical histories of the righteous predecessors, The Salafus-Salih. A companion once found an old sage painstakingly repairing a community wall in a city plagued by civil strife, insecurity, corruption, and failing governance.
“Ya Sheikh, why do you exhaust your remaining days fixing a wall for a city whose foundations are rotting and whose people have abandoned virtue?”
The sage did not stop his work. He wiped the sweat from his brow and replied:
“When the angels look down upon this city, let them find at least one soul building while everyone else is tearing down. I do not fix this wall because the city deserves it; I fix it because the Lord of this city demands righteousness from me, regardless of what the crowds choose to do.”
Dear brothers and sisters! Nigeria will not be saved by systemic overhauls alone. It will be saved when its citizens experience a psychological and spiritual awakening. It requires an ascetic detachment from immediate, selfish gains in exchange for the lasting legacy of a stable society.
Dear brothers and sisters! Let this be your reminder: You were placed in Nigeria by divine decree, not by accident. You will be questioned about what you did with the piece of earth allotted to you. Stand up, reform your heart, build your community, and put the survival of your homeland first.
Fellow Nigerians! Know that, the destiny of a nation is carved in the secret whispers of its citizens’ prayers. When hands are raised in sincere supplication for a homeland, a profound spiritual activation takes place—transforming despair into hope, friction into unity, and stagnation into progress.
Dear servants of Allah, O citizens of a land rich in soil, vibrant in spirit, and heavy with human potential!
Look around you. A nation is not merely a collection of borders, infrastructure, or political entities. A nation is a living soul, woven together by the collective hearts of its people. Nigeria—our home—stands at a monumental crossroads. We face trials that test our patience, economic hardships that strain our resolve, and fractures that threaten our unity. Yet, as Muslim believers, we do not despair. Despair is the language of the forgotten, and we belong to Al-Hayy, The Ever-Living and Al-Qayyum, The Sustainer of All Existences.
“And your Lord says, ‘Call upon Me; I will respond to you.'” [Qur’an, 40:60]
Remember, Du’a is not a last resort for the helpless; it is the ultimate weapon of the powerful. It is a spiritual catalyst capable of altering the Divine decree, shifting geopolitical realities, and softening the hardest of hearts.
Let us reflect on the profound wisdom of the great ascetic Islamic scholar, Imam Fudail Ibn Iyad (may Allah have mercy on him), who famously said:
“If I had a single supplication that was guaranteed to be answered, I would make it for none other than the leader, or the Sultan.” When asked why, he replied: “If I make the Du’a for myself, the benefit stops with me. But if I make it for the leader, and he is reformed, then through his righteousness, entire nations, communities, and citizens will find peace, justice, and prosperity.”
This is a heart-softening psychological shift. It is easy to criticise, to speak words of anger, and to curse those who govern. But anger breeds chaos; Du’a breeds rectification. Our leaders are human beings tested with immense burdens. When we pray for their guidance, their fear of Allah, and their wisdom, we are actively investing in our own security, our economy, and the future of our children.
We are a nation of diversity—a beautiful mosaic of tribes, tongues, and cultures. But diversity without a unifying spirit becomes a weapon of division. Allah Almighty commands us:
“And hold firmly to the rope of Allah all together and do not become divided.” [Qur’an, 3:103]
Progress cannot thrive in a house divided against itself. Our development relies on mutual empathy. We must make Du’a that Allah cleanses our hearts of tribalism, nepotism, and religious animosity, replacing them with collective patriotism and love for our neighbours.
Peace and economic sustenance are intertwined twins. Without peace, businesses cannot grow, farmers cannot harvest, and children cannot learn. We must beg Allah for security across every state, from the creeks to the savannahs. We must invoke His name, Ar-Razzaq, The Provider, to pour down His blessings upon Nigeria, turning our natural resources from tools of exploitation into streams of shared prosperity.
Raise your hands, clear your minds, and let your hearts cry out to the Lord of the Worlds with absolute certainty.
Ya Allah, Lord of the Heavens and the Earth! We turn to You on this day, acknowledging our shortcomings, but placing our absolute hope in Your infinite mercy. We ask You to grant complete, lasting, and beautiful peace to our nation, Nigeria.
Ya Allah, Safe-Keeper of the Vulnerable! Heal our lands from the wounds of insecurity, violence, banditry, and terrorism. Let every corner of Nigeria, from the North to the South, from the East to the West, become a sanctuary of safety, where the young can dream and the old can rest in tranquility.
Ya Allah, Guide of the Confused! We lay the affairs of our leaders before You. Ya Allah, touch the hearts of our President, our Governors, our Lawmakers, and our Traditional Rulers. Grant them profound wisdom, empathy, and an unwavering fear of You. Let them see leadership not as a privilege of luxury, but as a heavy trust and amanah for which they will be questioned on the Day of Judgment. Guide them to policies that alleviate poverty, foster justice, and drive sustainable development.
Ya Allah, Creator of Diversity! Unite our hearts as citizens. Eradicate the diseases of tribalism, regionalism, and hatred from our souls. Bind the citizens of Nigeria together with the cords of mutual respect, love, and common purpose. Let our diversity be our greatest strength, not our downfall.
Ya Allah, Ar-Razzaq, The All-Providing! Open the gates of sustenance for the millions of struggling households across Nigeria. Bless our farmers, our entrepreneurs, our workers, and our youths. Let our economy flourish through honest means. Deliver us from the hardships of inflation and scarcity, and grant us barakah and blessing in our resources.
Ya Allah! Uplift the spirit of the Nigerian youth. Grant them patience, focus, creativity, and avenues to excel so that they may build a brighter tomorrow.
Ya Allah! Do not punish us for the sins of the corrupt among us, but forgive us, rectify our state, and change our condition from hardship to ease.
Respected brothers and sisters! Wallahi, change never begins at the presidential villa; it begins in the mirror.
If we want an honest country, we must be honest in our market transactions. If we want a peaceful country, we must stop spreading malice on our social media platforms. Use this Du’a not just as words spoken, but as a blueprint for personal reformation.
Finally, I pray, may Allah Almighty heal the land of Nigeria, purify the hearts of all its leaders, bless all its citizens with prosperity, and make our love for righteousness greater than our fear of tyranny. Amin Ya Hayyu Ya Qayyum!
All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds. May the peace, blessings and salutations of Allah be upon our noble Messenger, Muhammad, and upon his family, his Companions and his true followers.
Murtadha Muhammad Gusau is the Chief Imam of Nagazi-Uvete Jumu’ah and the late Alhaji Abdur-Rahman Okene’s Mosques, Okene, Kogi State, Nigeria. He can be reached via: [email protected] or +2348038289761 or +2348024192217.
